explain.say: Look at the board. A calm-down corner is a quiet, cosy space. You go there to help your body calm down. Anyone can use it. It is a kind place that helps you.

explain.say: Here is what can go in a calm corner. Soft things are a cushion, a blanket and a soft toy. Calm tools are ear defenders, a squeeze ball, a book and a breathing card. With a grown-up, plan a calm corner at home.

faq.q: How do I know I need the calm corner?
faq.a: Check your body. A hot face, tight fists, a fluttery tummy or too much noise in your head are signs.
asks: Tell me about Notice my feeling

faq.q: What do I say to use the calm corner?
faq.a: You can say, Can I go to the calm corner, please? Some schools use a card you can show instead.
asks: Tell me about Ask to go

faq.q: How long do I stay in the calm corner?
faq.a: Usually a few minutes, until your body feels softer. A timer can help. Then you come back.

faq.q: Is the calm corner a punishment?
faq.a: No. It is a kind, quiet place to calm down. Anyone can use it.

faq.q: What goes in a calm corner?
faq.a: Soft things help, like a cushion and a blanket. Calm tools help too, like ear defenders, a squeeze ball and books.

facts: Many classrooms have a calm space where children can go to settle big feelings.
A calm corner works best when you use it before feelings get very big.

quiz.say: Aoife feels hot and cross in class. What can she do?
quiz.show: 😠 Aoife feels hot and cross. What can she do?

options.show: Ask to use the calm corner
options.say: Ask to use the calm corner

quiz.why: Asking gives Aoife a safe place to settle. Her teacher knows where she is.

wrong.0: Running out can worry her teacher, who wants to keep her safe.
wrong.2: Shouting can upset her friend and make the feeling bigger.

quiz.say: Sam feels steady again in the calm corner. What comes next?
quiz.show: Sam feels steady now. What comes next?
quiz.why: The calm corner is for a short time. When Sam feels ready, he joins in again.

wrong.0: The calm corner is a short stop, and Sam is ready to go back.
wrong.1: Sam already feels steady, so he is ready to join in.
